data.text: User-centered design involves users in the design and implementation to create usable software that meets the needs of laypersons. Since XR software is intended for users who may not need to know how the hardware or software works, it requires a structured, step-by-step software development lifecycle. Software engineering provides this systematic approach by building software in connected stages.
points: User-centered design involves users in the design and implementation to make software usable.
XR software is intended for laypersons who may not need to know how the hardware or software works.
Obtaining usable software requires a structured, step-by-step software development lifecycle.
Software engineering is a systematic process of building software in connected stages.

data.text: A design space is the set of all possible designs, and a calendar application has a very large design space. In most practical systems, a reasonably significant number of valid design choices can remain, even if many designs may be invalid. A software development life cycle (SDLC) is a systematic approach that helps identify the best valid design choice in terms of usability.
points: A design space is the set of all possible designs.
A calendar application has a very large design space.
In most practical systems, a reasonably significant number of valid design choices can remain, even if many designs may be invalid.
A software development life cycle (SDLC) is a systematic approach that helps identify the best valid design choice in terms of usability.

data.text: A software development lifecycle is a set of stages followed in a sequence where users must be involved in every stage of interactive system design. A highly iterative lifecycle is required for user-centric design because user needs and expectations create loops back to previous stages. These iterations account for user feedback in different ways, including a design-prototype-evaluate cycle that can iterate back to requirement gathering.
points: A software development lifecycle is a set of stages followed in a sequence.
Users must be involved in every stage of interactive system design.
A highly iterative lifecycle is required for user-centric design because user needs create loops back to previous stages.
Iterations between stages are intended to account for user feedback in different ways.
The lifecycle includes various stages, such as a design-prototype-evaluate cycle that iterates back to requirement gathering.

data.text: End users and the client must be involved from the requirement-gathering stage onwards using methods like contextual inquiry, ethnographic studies, and cultural probes. The design-prototype-evaluate loop then uses user feedback to iteratively refine interface and interaction designs until they are stabilized. Because code design is a separate later activity, these loops must be completed quickly to avoid significant increases in overall turnaround time.
points: End users and the client must be involved from the requirement-gathering stage onwards.
Requirements can be gathered using contextual inquiry, ethnographic studies, and cultural probes.
The design-prototype-evaluate loop refines interface and interaction designs using user feedback until they are stabilized.
Each loop must be completed quickly to prevent the overall turnaround time from increasing significantly.

data.text: Coding and code testing follow traditional software engineering, where fewer iterations are preferred because code design is costly. The iterative life cycle includes three evaluation points: early evaluation, code testing, and empirical study. While code testing ensures the system is executable, empirical studies are required to ensure usability and typically distinguish interactive systems from other software development.
points: Coding and code testing follow traditional software engineering, where fewer iterations are preferred because code design is costly.
The iterative software development life cycle includes three evaluation points: early evaluation, code testing, and empirical study.
Code testing ensures the system is executable and bug-free, but empirical studies are required to ensure usability with end users.
Empirical studies are typically not part of other software development and differentiate interactive systems by involving end users.

data.text: In the iterative design of usable extended reality systems, the design-prototype-evaluate cycle is the only loop designed to be performed quickly. Frequent loops other than this cycle significantly affect a project's outcome, cost, and turnaround time. Development stages should be completed carefully so that the need to return to previous stages does not arise.
points: The design-prototype-evaluate cycle is the only loop designed to be performed quickly.
Frequent loops other than the design-prototype-evaluate cycle significantly affect a project's outcome, cost, and turnaround time.
Development stages should be completed carefully so that the need to return to previous stages does not arise.

data.text: Building interactive software is broadly similar to building regular software, but the differences are in the requirement gathering, design-prototype-evaluate, and empirical study stages. The book Human-Computer Interaction, User-Centric Computing for Design discusses these stages in more detail with respect to broader interactive system development concerns.
points: Building interactive software is broadly similar to building regular software except for specific development stages.
The book Human-Computer Interaction, User-Centric Computing for Design discusses these stages in more detail regarding broader concerns.
